[2026-09-23T17:00:39.694037+00:00] CLAIM: the mist on raised ground. His screenshot stands at level 2 inside a 90%-mist marsh and shows none. The existing gate (verify-mistzone) deliberately picks LOW ground — "a mist zone on a summit shows nothing" — so no arm has ever looked at the band where the effect collapses. [2026-09-23T18:50:37.665109+00:00] THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLED IT. MIST_FRAG hugs the ground with pool = 1 - (z - 0.4) * 0.5, measured from SEA LEVEL. Mean pool over the world's five 90-share mist zones: tarn (median level 32) 0.000, southern lake (12) 0.000, meadow (4) 0.010, his marsh (2) 0.196, heath (0) 0.763. FOUR OF FIVE PAINTED NOTHING — maps2 put mist on lakes, tarns, marshes and meadows, which is exactly right, and a tarn is a MOUNTAIN lake. The floor is now each zone's own MEDIAN ground level (not the minimum: one stray low cell inside a zone would drag it back to the sea), computed once per zone from __ml.levelAt and cached by id. At his stand 305,140 level 2: painted fraction 42% -> 90%, drawMax 0.148 (band 1, the faintest, nothing above it) -> 0.740 (the top band), drawMean 0.0625 -> 0.581. Level 0 is bit-identical: verify-mistzone still reads 0.74/0.707 deep inside the heath.

[2026-09-23T18:50:37.665109+00:00] A TWIN CANNOT SEE THE SHADER, and this is the sharpest form of the charter's pixel law I have hit. __ml.mistDrawAt is an EXACT JS twin of MIST_FRAG — which makes it a perfect instrument for everything except "did the GLSL change". A mutant pinning the shader's floor back to sea level PASSED every counter arm of my new gate (max 0.74, mean 0.36, painted 0.72 at the tarn) because the arms read the twin and the twin still had the floor. The frame arm added: mean centre luma, clear vs fog. Fixed build 12.1 / 18.9 / 78.9 / 57.2 / 19.8 luma at levels 0/2/4/12/32; the mutant 12.1 / 1.53 / 0.26 / -0.01 / -0.83 — the level-0 control passes under the mutant, correctly, because its floor IS 0. Any gate over a shader with a CPU twin needs a frame arm; the twin arms cannot fail.

[2026-09-23T18:50:37.665109+00:00] THE GATE'S BLIND SPOT WAS WRITTEN DOWN AS A LAW. verify-mistzone picks its stands on LOW ground on purpose — its own comment says "a mist zone on a summit shows nothing" — and ambient/README.md had that as a TRAP note: "the banks pool on ground at level <= ~2 and nowhere else ... of the five 90-share mist zones only the south-eastern green (level 0) can show it; the gate stands there". [2026-09-23T18:50:37.665109+00:00] FOUR HARNESS TRAPS PAID FOR, all worth copying. (1) A PROBE RESOLVED ONCE AT CONSTRUCTION captures undefined — the ambient mount runs before WorldScene publishes __ml, so levelFromProbe() returning a value instead of a closure floored every zone at 0 forever, silently, with refMax 0 the only sign; pickFromProbe looks up per call and that is why. And an UNMEASURED floor is never cached, or one early miss pins a zone at sea level for the session. (2) THE 4-SECOND GLOOM ROLL IS NOT 4 SECONDS IN A HEADLESS PAGE: easeGloom is driven by game.loop.delta, the CLAMPED physics dt whose call site already warns it "would crawl on slow clients" (time-of-day was moved to the wall clock for exactly this). Measured: 0.5 s of delta accumulated in 21 s of wall clock, mist still at 0.88. Gates must SNAP (__ml.weather(idx, true)), never wait. (3) A SKY FORCE IS A SERVER ROUND TRIP: snapping in the same breath as worldAmbient([]) snaps back to the zone field, so the "clear" control measured the fog it was the absence of — wait for zone().ruled to agree, and a release that silently fails degrades every later stand. (4) A PER-PIXEL ENVELOPE CANNOT SURVIVE THIS SCREEN (ground RT slices plus a dozen moving effects): it read 0.000 beyond noise at a heath painting mean alpha 0.73. For a big soft effect the statistic is MEAN CENTRE LUMA, as verify-mistrow already had it.

[2026-09-23T19:11:52.500426+00:00] REBASE ONTO games-perf's ZONEFIELD REWRITE, resolved with both intents. They had rebuilt zonefield.ts (bbox index, one pass, numeric keys, two generations, an incremental raster memo) and mount.ts under me. My floor started as a SECOND full 64x40 walk whose owner test scanned all 96 zone polygons per texel — precisely the cost they had just removed — so it was folded into THEIR walk instead: raster(name, rect, cols, rows, refOut?) fills mask and floor in one pass, the overlap memo carries the floor through, and the floor's holes take the same four neighbour passes as the mask (an unknown left at 0 is a SEA-LEVEL hole punched through a raised zone, over exactly the cliff faces the mask's fill exists for). floorAt reads the holders out of their per-cell memo, so it costs no box test and no polygon test — only the owner rule over the 1-3 zones covering the cell. Gates on the REBASED tree: verify-misthigh OK (all five zones, floors 0/2/4/12/36), verify-zonefield OK, verify-mistrow OK, 26 unit tests, typecheck green. NOTE FOR WHOEVER RUNS verify-mistzone: it needs a LOW mist zone whose ten-minute window has mist on, and the heath is the only one — so it is unrunnable about one window in ten and says 'could not stand outside a low mist zone with mist on' when it is. Confirmed against the roll, not a regression. verify-misthigh has no such hole: its zone-driven arm skips loudly and its forced arm is deterministic. ALSO: never run two browser gates against one dev stack — they teleport and force the sky under each other, and that is what made verify-mistrow read -5.4 luma.

[2026-09-23T19:32:09.869421+00:00] "THE BOX DOES NOT CHANGE THE PRICE" WAS TRUE, AND I WROTE IT DOWN AS A LAW. My 2026-09-13 note said frequency was the ONLY honest lever on __ml.objectsIn, because it walks every object on screen and filters afterwards. That was a description of the probe's shape, not a fact about the problem — and it stopped me looking for a year of commits. The probe is a QA instrument one feature has to call for real: it paid a getBounds() and an eleven-field record with two string slices and three toFixed for EVERY visible image, then sorted the lot, and pairPieces threw ~95% away (967 returned, 16 of them s3:). Moving a string compare ahead of the transform and the allocation is 21x. LESSON: when a doc says the only lever is X, check whether that is a property of the problem or of the code you happened to write. games-perf suggested a spatial index; it is not needed — measure the cheap fix first.
